newsitem.title: USA: Rollins head says disappointed with results.
newsitem.headline: Rollins head says disappointed with results.

text.p: Rollins Inc's president and chief operating officer, Gary Rollins, said the company was disappointed with results this year.
In a statement, Rollins said noted, however, that implementation of the company's strategic plans to address the company's core businesses "will allow us to realize significant long-term bernefits."
He said the plans have emphasis on recurring revenue, the commercial segment, new termite warranties, and marketing.

Rollins owns and operates Orkin Exterminating Co Inc, which offers termite and pest control services, and provides lawn care and plantscaping services; and Rollins Protective Services, which provides electronic security systems.

Earlier, Rollins reported results for the year ended December 31. It said its revenues increased 1.1 percent to to $627,431,000 while net income dropped 42.0 percent to $22,795,000. This resulted in earnings per share of $0.64 compared to $1.10 a year ago.
It said the year's performance was negatively impacted by investments in expansion and growth related programs and a " substandard" termite season.

It said that for the year, Orkin's revenues increased 1.0 percent while operating income decreased 49.4 percent. It said Orkin had an increase in customers and recurring pest control and termite renewal revenues, but those gains were offset by the decrease in termite sales.
The unit's operating income for the year was hurt by branch and region openings, investments in the new Commercial Division, insurance costs, and termite claims, it said.
The quarter's results were likewise influenced by the same contributing factors, it said.
Rollins Protective Services' revenues increased 7.5 percent and operating income dropped 10.8 percent for the year.
It said the unit's earnings reflected the impact of investments in new dedicated commercial branches, related market development, and costs associated with acquisitions.
